このパソコンが使えます。

words.meaning: and; one of several reasons (after a predicate)
words.example: 近いし、時給もいいです。

words.meaning: if it is; as for that case

lessons.title: Can you work here?
lessons.description: Read a café job notice, explain your abilities and availability, and try a task before accepting it.
lessons.canDo: Find the conditions in a job notice and explain what I can do

grammar.title: Abilities and frequency
grammar.formation: Godan: final u-row → e-row + る (話す → 話せる). Ichidan: drop る + られる (食べる → 食べられる). する → できる; 来る → 来られる. Period + に + number + 回.
grammar.explanation: Potential forms state an ability or possibility. Use が for the thing you can do in these examples; を is also used with many potential verbs. The polite negative is ～えません / ～られません. 一週間に三回 gives frequency, while 三時間 gives duration. Colloquial 食べれる exists, but learn 食べられる as the standard form first.
grammar.example: 日本語が少し話せます。
grammar.translation: I can speak a little Japanese.

examples.ja: {週末|しゅうまつ}は{働|はたら}けますが、{月曜日|げつようび}は{働|はたら}けません。
examples.en: I can work on weekends, but not on Mondays.

examples.ja: {一週間|いっしゅうかん}に{三回|さんかい}{来|き}られます。
examples.en: I can come three times a week.

examples.ja: {注文|ちゅうもん}が{聞|き}けます。
examples.en: I can take orders (listen to customers' orders).

grammar.mistake: 働きます says that you work; 働けます says that you can. 三回 is three occasions, not three hours.

grammar.title: Reasons and first impressions
grammar.formation: Plain predicate + し (noun / な-adjective + だし; polite forms + し also work). い-adjective: drop い + そう; な-adjective stem + そう. いい → よさそう; ない → なさそう.
grammar.explanation: し lists reasons and often leaves room for others: 近いし、時給もいいです. Stem + そう describes a visible impression rather than certain knowledge. おいしそう means it looks tasty, without claiming you have tasted it. Do not confuse this with plain-form + そうです for reported information, introduced later.
grammar.example: 近いし、時給もいいです。
grammar.translation: It's nearby, and the hourly pay is good too.

examples.ja: {店|みせ}は{近|ちか}いし、バスもあります。
examples.en: The shop is nearby, and there is a bus too.

examples.ja: このケーキはおいしそうです。
レンさんは{忙|いそが}しそうです。

grammar.mistake: おいしいそうです reports that someone said it is tasty; おいしそうです describes how it looks.

grammar.title: Try it; explain the relevant case
grammar.formation: Verb て-form + みる (作ってみる). Noun or plain clause + なら (週末なら; 働くなら).
grammar.explanation: ～てみる is trying an action to see what it is like, not merely making an unsuccessful attempt. なら takes up a case already mentioned: 週末なら働けます means weekends work for me. It does not promise that the action happens automatically whenever the condition occurs.
grammar.translation: If it's on the weekend, I can work.

examples.ja: コーヒーを{作|つく}ってみます。
{週末|しゅうまつ}なら{働|はたら}けます。
examples.en: If it's weekends, I can work.

examples.ja: この{店|みせ}で{働|はたら}くなら、レンさんに{連絡|れんらく}してください。
examples.en: If you want to work at this shop, please contact Ren.

grammar.mistake: Use 作ってみる, not 作るみる. なら responds to a relevant case; it is not a general replacement for every English 'if'.

dialogues.title: At Ren's café
dialogues.scene: You have read the café notice. Ren asks about your abilities and when you can work.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: こんにちは。{今日|きょう}は{面接|めんせつ}ですね。{日本語|にほんご}が{話|はな}せますか。
lines.romaji: Konnichiwa. Kyō wa mensetsu desu ne. Nihongo ga hanasemasu ka.
lines.meaning: Hello. Today is your interview, isn't it? Can you speak Japanese?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {少|すこ}し{話|はな}せます。{注文|ちゅうもん}も{聞|き}けます。
lines.meaning: I can speak a little. I can take orders too.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: {一週間|いっしゅうかん}に{何回|なんかい}{働|はたら}けますか。
lines.meaning: How many times a week can you work?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {三回|さんかい}です。{週末|しゅうまつ}なら、{長|なが}い{時間|じかん}{働|はたら}けます。
lines.romaji: Sankai desu. Shūmatsu nara, nagai jikan hatarakemasu.
lines.meaning: Three times. On weekends, I can work longer hours.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: {月曜日|げつようび}の{午後|ごご}はどうですか。
lines.romaji: Getsuyōbi no gogo wa dō desu ka.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {授業|じゅぎょう}があるので、{月曜日|げつようび}は{働|はたら}けません。{夏|なつ}は{時間|じかん}があります。
lines.romaji: Jugyō ga aru node, getsuyōbi wa hatarakemasen. Natsu wa jikan ga arimasu.
lines.meaning: I have class, so I can't work on Mondays. In summer I have time.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: わかりました。では、{今度|こんど}コーヒーを{作|つく}ってみましょう。
lines.romaji: Wakarimashita. Dewa, kondo kōhī o tsukutte mimashō.
lines.meaning: Understood. Then let's try making coffee next time.

dialogues.title: Trying the machine
dialogues.scene: On your next visit Ren shows you the coffee machine. You explain why the job appeals to you.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: この{機械|きかい}が{使|つか}えますか。

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {初|はじ}めてです。{使|つか}ってみてもいいですか。
lines.romaji: Hajimete desu. Tsukatte mite mo ii desu ka.
lines.meaning: It's my first time. May I try using it?

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: はい。ここを{押|お}してください。これでコーヒーが{作|つく}れます。
lines.romaji: Hai. Koko o oshite kudasai. Kore de kōhī ga tsukuremasu.
lines.meaning: Yes. Please press here. You can make coffee with this.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: いいにおいですね。あのケーキもおいしそうです。
lines.romaji: Ii nioi desu ne. Ano kēki mo oishisō desu.
lines.meaning: It smells good. That cake looks tasty too.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: どうして、この{店|みせ}で{働|はたら}きたいんですか。
lines.romaji: Dōshite, kono mise de hatarakitai n desu ka.
lines.meaning: Why do you want to work at this shop?

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {近|ちか}いし、バスもあるし、{時給|じきゅう}もいいからです。
lines.romaji: Chikai shi, basu mo aru shi, jikyū mo ii kara desu.
lines.meaning: Because it's nearby, there's a bus, and the hourly pay is good.

lines.speaker: Ren
lines.line: そうですか。{時間|じかん}があるときに、また{来|き}てください。{今度|こんど}はケーキも{作|つく}ってみましょう。
lines.romaji: Sō desu ka. Jikan ga aru toki ni, mata kite kudasai. Kondo wa kēki mo tsukutte mimashō.
lines.meaning: I see. Please come again when you have time. Next time let's try making cake too.

readings.title: Café recruitment notice
paragraphs: カフェのアルバイトを{募集|ぼしゅう}しています。
{一週間|いっしゅうかん}に{三回|さんかい}{働|はたら}ける{人|ひと}を{募集|ぼしゅう}しています。
{週末|しゅうまつ}の{午後|ごご}に{働|はたら}ける{人|ひと}がいいです。
{時給|じきゅう}は{千二百円|せんにひゃくえん}です。
{経験|けいけん}がなくても{大丈夫|だいじょうぶ}です。
{面接|めんせつ}は{金曜日|きんようび}の{午後|ごご}{三時|さんじ}です。
メールでレンに{連絡|れんらく}してください。

watch.prompt: Optionally watch a short café or workplace scene. Save one line expressing ability or availability and note who is speaking. Do not guess a speaker's intention from grammar alone.

exercises.prompt: When can the applicant work longer hours?
exercises.explain: 週末なら、長い時間働けます explicitly gives weekends. Summer is when they have time, but it is not their only availability.

exercises.prompt: Why can't the applicant work on Mondays?
exercises.explain: 授業があるので gives the reason: they have class.

exercises.prompt: What does Ren suggest trying on the next visit?
exercises.explain: 今度はケーキも作ってみましょう: next time let's try making cake too.

exercises.context: Explain your ability to speak a little Japanese.
exercises.line: {日本語|にほんご}が{少|すこ}し＿＿。
exercises.explain: 話せます is the potential form. The others describe past actions or their absence, not ability.

exercises.context: Say you can work three times per week.
exercises.line: {一週間|いっしゅうかん}＿＿{三回|さんかい}{働|はたら}けます。
exercises.explain: A period + に + a count expresses frequency: three occasions per week.

exercises.line: {週末|しゅうまつ}に{働|はたら}けますか。
options: いいえ、{週末|しゅうまつ}は{働|はたら}けません。
{週末|しゅうまつ}は{昨日|きのう}でした。
はい、{週末|しゅうまつ}なら{働|はたら}けます。
exercises.context: You can work weekends. Choose the reply that communicates that availability.
exercises.explain: The first reply confirms the stated availability. The negative reply would communicate the opposite.

exercises.line: この{機械|きかい}が{使|つか}えますか。
exercises.context: You have never used it and want permission to try. Choose that reply.
options: {初|はじ}めてです。{使|つか}ってみてもいいですか。
{昨日|きのう}から{使|つか}っています。
exercises.explain: 初めてです explains it is your first time; 使ってみてもいいですか asks permission to try.

exercises.meaning: If it's weekends, I can work.
exercises.explain: Take up the relevant case with なら, then state your ability.

exercises.prompt: You haven't tasted the cake. Which describes only its visible impression?
options: おいしくありませんでした。
exercises.explain: おいしそう describes how it looks. The two past statements imply an assessment of its taste.

exercises.context: List proximity and good hourly pay as two reasons.
exercises.line: {近|ちか}い＿＿、{時給|じきゅう}もいいです。
exercises.explain: し connects reasons after a predicate; 近いし is the correct form.

exercises.prompt: When does the applicant say they have time?
exercises.explain: 夏は時間があります explicitly says they have time in summer.
The て-form + みる means trying an action to see what it is like: 乗ってみます. The bus is available in the scene.
exercises.context: Try taking the bus once to find out what the journey is like.

exercises.prompt: How much is the advertised hourly pay?
exercises.explain: 時給は千二百円です states 1,200 yen per hour.

exercises.prompt: How should an applicant contact Ren?
exercises.explain: メールでレンに連絡してください gives the contact method.

exercises.prompt: Which applicant can apply according to the notice?
options: Only someone with three years of experience
Only someone who has made cakes professionally
exercises.explain: 経験がなくても大丈夫です explicitly permits applicants without prior experience.
金曜日の午後三時 gives Friday, three in the afternoon.
